stem: Donor A has 49 rooted of 50 cuttings while Donor B has 31 rooted of 50 at the same validated time point. What is the strongest first interpretation?
choices: Treat the donor-linked difference as meaningful and investigate donor history, condition, handling, and environment without yet assigning a genetic cause.
Average the two donor groups into one facility rooting rate because both were produced under the same propagation process.
Treat Donor B as genetically inferior because the rooting difference is large and appears at the same validated endpoint.
Exclude unrooted cuttings from the denominator because the comparison should focus on viable propagules.
rationale: A 49/50 versus 31/50 result at the same validated endpoint is a real donor-linked performance difference, but the pattern does not by itself identify why it occurred. Donor condition, cutting quality, handling, sanitation, rooting environment, source-plant history, and genotype may all contribute. The strongest interpretation preserves the donor-group difference and investigates competing explanations rather than averaging it away or declaring genetic failure prematurely.
